overview: The Council approved a resolution condemning the killing of a bystander by federal immigration agents in Minneapolis and referred the development of local safety protocols to committee. The body also authorized $300,000 for a school feasibility study and passed a first reading of an ordinance banning municipal use of face surveillance technology.

items.title: Resolution on the passing of Clarence Ed Ligon Jr.
items.summary: Approved a resolution expressing condolences to the family of Clarence Ed Ligon Jr. and held a moment of silence for the community leader.

items.title: Meeting Records and License Approvals
items.summary: Approved the records of the January 6, 2026 meeting and granted a common victualler's license to Annie's Pizzeria.

items.title: Committee Reports on EMS and City Clerk Hiring
items.summary: Approved committee reports regarding a requested pause on ambulance service changes and the recruitment process for the City Clerk position.

items.title: Executive Session: De Silva v. City of Medford
items.summary: The Council entered executive session to discuss strategy regarding the litigation of De Silva v. City of Medford.

items.title: Capital Stabilization Fund: Roberts Elementary Study
items.summary: Approved a $300,000 appropriation for a feasibility study and design costs for a potential roof and heat pump replacement project at Roberts Elementary School.

items.title: Committee of the Whole on School Building Projects
items.summary: Approved a motion to hold a committee meeting with the administration and public school representatives to review the status and funding of several ongoing school building projects.

items.title: Resolution Condemning the Killing of Renee Nicole Goode
items.summary: Approved a resolution condemning the death of a bystander during a federal immigration action in Minneapolis and referred the development of safety protocols for documenting law enforcement activity to the Public Health and Community Safety Committee. Councilors and numerous residents discussed community fear, the role of local police during federal actions, and the need for clear guidelines to protect residents' rights and safety.

items.title: Resolution to Increase City Employee Vacation Time
items.summary: Referred a proposal to amend the municipal code to increase vacation time for employees in their first five years of service to the Administration and Finance Committee.

items.title: Ordinance Banning Face Surveillance Technology
items.summary: Passed for first reading an ordinance that prohibits city departments from using, acquiring, or accessing face surveillance technology.
